# stackit_resourcemanager_folder_iam_policy_v1 (Resource)

IAM policy resource schema.

~> This resource is part of the experimental feature iam and is likely going to undergo significant changes or be removed in the future. Use it at your own discretion.

~> Destruction of the IAM policy resource will only remove it from the state and won't modify the IAM policy on API side. Previous listed subjects will keep their role bindings.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "stackit_resourcemanager_folder_iam_policy_v1" "iam_policy" {
  resource_id = "xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx"
  role_bindings = [
    {
      role        = "owner"
      subject     = "john.doe@example.com"
    }
    {
      role        = "editor"
      subject     = "jane.doe@example.com"
    }
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `resource_id` (String) The identifier of the resource to apply this IAM policy to.
- `role_bindings` (Attributes List) The role bindings of the policy. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--role_bindings))

### Read-Only

- `etag` (String) Internal etag used for API concurrency control.
- `id` (String) Terraform's internal resource identifier. It is structured as "`resource_id`".

<a id="nestedatt--role_bindings"></a>
### Nested Schema for `role_bindings`

Required:

- `role` (String) A valid role defined for the resource.
- `subject` (String) Identifier of user, service account or client. Usually email address or name in case of clients.

## Import

```terraform
# Only use the import statement if you want to import an existing role binding
import {
  to = stackit_resourcemanager_folder_iam_policy_v1.import_example
  id = "${var.resource_id}"
}
```
